model_and_data: The extract studies learning an unknown function on the d-dimensional sphere by ridge regression on N random features. The feature formula in that quote is broken after σ(wT. A later quote describes the random-features model as a randomized approximation to kernel ridge regression or as a two-layer neural network with random first-layer weights; that line spells the last word “wights”. The functions in FRF(Θ) are quoted as two-layer neural networks except that the first layer is kept constant, and the method is quoted as a finite-rank approximation to kernel ridge regression. Covariates are quoted as i.i.d. uniform on Sd−1; the radius display is not on that line. Random features (θi) are quoted as i.i.d. uniform on a sphere. The response quote is yi = fd(xi) + εi, with εi independent of xi and Eε(ε1) = 0; the second-moment display breaks after Eε(ε2 and continues “1) = τ 2”. A quoted linear regression function is fd(x) = βd,0 + ⟨βd,1, x⟩. The proportional regime is quoted as N, n, d →∞ with N/d →ψ1 and n/d →ψ2 for some ψ1, ψ2 ∈(0, ∞).
loss: The coefficients a = (ai)i≤N are learned by ridge regression. The quoted test error, also called prediction error and, with the extract’s stated slight abuse of terminology, generalization error, is the mean squared error of predicting fd(x) for x uniform on the sphere. The same definition’s quote says this quantity does not take the expectation over the training data X, the random features Θ, or the data noise ε, and that the risk concentrates; that sentence is cut off in the quote.
varied_axis: These are separate quoted axes. One quote plots prediction error as a function of the number of parameters per dimension ψ1 = N/d. The interpolation-threshold peak is quoted at ψ1 = ψ2. Another quote plots predicted test error as a function of ψ1/ψ2 = N/n, for fixed ψ2, several values of λ > 0, and two values of the SNR. A quoted ReLU caption fixes the rescaled sample size at n/d ≡ψ2 = 10 and uses different curves for different regularization λ. Further quoted limits of the asymptotic formula, listed on their own lines, are the highly overparametrized regime ψ1 →∞ and the large-sample limit ψ2 →∞. The next line says those limits are taken after N, n, d →∞ with N/d →∞ and n/d →∞. That ratio display is ambiguous next to the finite positive ψ1, ψ2 in the proportional-regime quote, and it is not repaired. The ridgeless limit λ →0 is a separate quoted object, not the same axis as ψ1.
held_fixed_axes: The quoted theorems require λ > 0 fixed as N, n, d →∞. A quoted ReLU caption fixes n/d ≡ψ2 = 10 while λ changes across curves. A quoted ReLU line uses σ(x) = max{x, 0} and ψ2 = n/d = 3 for that comparison. Assumption 1 quotes a weakly differentiable activation, and the bound is printed as c0ec1|u| for finite constants c0, c1. These holdings are the ones in the quoted theorem or figure, not one global list for every display.
interpolation_definition: The interpolation threshold is quoted as the model-complexity threshold above which the training error vanishes (the model completely interpolates the data). In this model that peak is quoted at ψ1 = ψ2. A quoted ReLU comparison uses minimum ℓ2-norm least squares as the λ →0 limit of Eq. (2), beside regularized least squares at λ = 10−3. Remark 1 quotes that the theorems require λ > 0 fixed in the diverging limit, and that sending λ →0 afterwards does not necessarily yield the prediction risk of the min-norm least squares estimator given by ˆa(0+) ≡limλ→0 ˆa(λ) at N, n, d. The next quoted line begins “fixed.” Gradient flow on the quoted mean squared error, starting at a = 0, is said to converge to the ridgeless limit (λ →0) of ˆa(λ), with a quoted correspondence between positive λ and early stopping in gradient descent.
assumptions: Assumption 1 lets σ : R →R be weakly differentiable, with weak derivative σ′, and the quote continues the bound as |σ(u)|, |σ′(u)| ≤ c0ec1|u| for some constants c0, c1 < ∞.
Assumption 2 defines ψ1,d = N/d and ψ2,d = n/d and assumes the following limits exist in (0, ∞).
The proportional-regime quote takes N, n, d →∞ with N/d →ψ1 and n/d →ψ2 for some ψ1, ψ2 ∈(0, ∞).
Assumption 3 assumes yi = fd(xi)+εi, with (εi) i.i.d. from Pε independent of (xi), and Eε(ε1) = 0.
The response quote writes yi = fd(xi) + εi with εi independent of xi and Eε(ε1) = 0, and the next line of that quote is “1) = τ 2”.
The functions in FRF(Θ) are two-layer neural networks, except that the first layer is kept constant.
Random features (θi)i≤N are i.i.d. uniform on a sphere; the radius continuation is outside this quote.
Remark 1 says Theorem 1 and its generalizations require λ > 0 fixed as N, n, d →∞.
The quoted remark says that taking λ →0 does not necessarily yield the prediction risk of the min-norm estimator ˆa(0+) at N, n, d.
The later-limit quote says the ψ1 →∞ and ψ2 →∞ limits are taken after N, n, d →∞ with N/d →∞ and n/d →∞. That ratio wording is left as printed.
result_type: Both an asymptotic statement and finite-d numerical comparisons. For linear fd and any λ > 0, the quote says the prediction risk convergences in probability; the limit display is not on those two lines and is not reconstructed. Theorem 2 is quoted as giving, for any λ > 0, the asymptotic prediction error of random-features ridge regression. Figure 1 is quoted as comparing the theoretical prediction with numerical results for several dimensions d, averaged over 20 instances.
transfer_limits: The estimator in the quotes is random-features ridge regression: a two-layer network whose first layer is kept constant, also described as a finite-rank approximation to kernel ridge regression. A separate quote about an earlier linear covariates model says that linear model is not directly connected to neural networks which are highly nonlinear in the covariates. Random forests are named in a citation that double descent was demonstrated empirically for random forests and random features. The extract does not locate gradient-boosted trees, a decision-tree experiment of this paper, or an essay corpus. A learned first layer is outside the quoted estimator, which keeps that layer constant.
